title: FastAPI REST Services & Routing Engine Integration
goal: Build the FastAPI backend application, integrate with OSRM/ORS for route generation, build PostGIS spatial snapping & incident intersection, and expose public REST APIs for route intelligence.

issues.title: [Sprint 2] FastAPI Core Architecture, CORS, Health Checks & Pydantic v2 Schemas
issues.description: Initialize Python 3.11+ FastAPI application skeleton under `backend/app/`. Configure asynchronous database session management with SQLAlchemy 2.0 / asyncpg. Set up CORS middleware, environment configuration via pydantic-settings, and standard response envelopes with meta timestamps.
acceptance_criteria: FastAPI app boots with `/api/v1/health` endpoint returning 200 OK and database connectivity status
CORS properly configured for local frontend origin (http://localhost:5173)
Pydantic v2 schemas defined for coordinates, route requests, segment summaries, and incidents
OpenAPI /docs swagger page cleanly renders all schemas and endpoints

issues.title: [Sprint 2] Routing Engine Integration (OSRM / OpenRouteService)
issues.description: Implement `RoutingService` in `backend/app/services/routing.py` that interfaces with OSRM or OpenRouteService API. Given start and destination coordinates, retrieve drivable GeoJSON LineString geometries, turn steps, distance in meters, and base duration.
acceptance_criteria: Service queries OSRM/ORS and parses route geometry into valid GeoJSON LineStrings
Handles route alternatives when requested (`include_alternatives=True`)
Validates origin and destination to ensure coordinates lie within Metro Manila bounding box
Gracefully handles unreachable coordinates or external routing timeouts with clean HTTP 400/502 errors

issues.title: [Sprint 2] Route Road-Segment Snapping & Spatial Intersect Service (PostGIS)
issues.description: Build spatial analysis service in `backend/app/services/spatial.py`. Given a route LineString geometry, execute PostGIS queries (`ST_DWithin`, `ST_Intersects`, `ST_LineLocatePoint`) to identify the specific `road_segments` traversed, compute traversed length per segment, and identify any active `incidents` within a 50-meter buffer.
acceptance_criteria: Identifies and orders road segments matching the route geometry from start to finish
Finds all active incidents within 50m buffer of the route line
Calculates baseline free-flow travel time versus observed traffic travel time per segment
Execution time for route spatial matching is < 80ms

issues.title: [Sprint 2] Route Intelligence Analysis Endpoint (`POST /api/v1/route/analyze`)
issues.description: Implement the core endpoint `POST /api/v1/route/analyze` combining routing, spatial segment matching, real-time telemetry extraction, travel delay computation, and incident diagnostics into the standard response payload defined in SPEC.md Section 4.1.
acceptance_criteria: Endpoint accepts start/dest names and coordinates and returns comprehensive route intelligence JSON
Computes estimated travel time, baseline travel time, and delay (+/- minutes)
Identifies the single 'most affected road segment' along the route
Returns constituent segments with individual speed, severity level, and attached incidents
API response time under 1200ms

issues.title: [Sprint 2] Traffic Heatmap, Incidents & City Dashboard REST Endpoints
issues.description: Implement auxiliary telemetry endpoints: `GET /api/v1/traffic/heatmap` (GeoJSON FeatureCollection of all road segments with current speeds), `GET /api/v1/incidents` (filtered list of active incidents with coordinates), and `GET /api/v1/dashboard/stats` (Metro Manila aggregate stats, active incident counts, most congested corridors).
acceptance_criteria: `/api/v1/traffic/heatmap` returns valid GeoJSON ready for MapLibre layer consumption
`/api/v1/incidents` supports filtering by city, incident type, and status
`/api/v1/dashboard/stats` returns active incidents count, severe roads count, and top 4 congested roads
Pytest integration tests pass for all endpoints
